I am 63 years old and I have never been to school, not even one day. But I have farmed these fields for 40 years since I was a young bride of 23, and I know what works with my own two hands. My husband and I work our 7.5 mu together — just the two of us, no hired help. We have a well, so water is not our biggest worry, but every bag of fertilizer and every bottle of pesticide is real money out of our pocket.

I split my land the same way I have done for decades. Five mu I do wheat-maize rotation, just like everyone else in our village. The other 2.5 mu I plant cotton. I do not change this. Why would I? It has fed us for 40 years.

For the winter wheat on my 5 mu, I plant around October 10th. I use Shimai or Lumai — whatever improved variety seed the dealer has that my neighbors bought last year and said was good. I need about half a bag of seed per mu, that is 30 jin, about 15 kg. Before planting, I run the rotary tiller over the field to make the soil fine. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the red bag they call 18-22-5, that is 50 kg. Then in the spring, when the wheat turns green, I spread another 100 jin of ammonium bicarbonate per mu. I would rather put a little too much than too little — if I lose the wheat crop, I lose everything. The fertilizer money is painful to spend, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I irrigate four times: once when I plant, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide three times, usually when I see aphids or the leaves start looking rusty. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu, this year I expect about 950 jin, around 950 kg per mu.

For the summer maize on the same 5 mu, as soon as the wheat comes off the field in early June, I plant hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble without plowing — no time to waste. I buy the seed in packages, about one package per mu, that is roughly 1.5 kg. I put down one bag of maize compound fertilizer per mu — the 27-6-7 kind, 50 kg. That is enough for maize, it is not as greedy as people think if you give it a good start. I irrigate twice: once right after planting because June can be dry, and once at tasseling when the ears are setting. I spray twice for pests. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, that is 1000 kg per mu.

For cotton on my 2.5 mu, I plant in late April. I use Guoxinmian seed, about 3 jin per mu, that is 1.5 kg. I till with the rotary tiller first because cotton likes loose soil. I put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg. Cotton is the most troublesome crop. I have to spray many times for bollworms and aphids — maybe 10 or 12 times through the summer. I irrigate three times. Picking is all by hand, just me and my husband bending over the plants. Last year I got about 500 jin per mu of seed cotton, around 500 kg per mu. I hope for the same this year.

I watch what my neighbors do. If they buy more fertilizer this year, I might buy a little more too. But I do not change much — I have done it this way for decades and it has not failed me yet. Spending more on fertilizer means less money for medicine or for fixing the roof, but I would still rather waste some fertilizer than risk losing my yield.
